verdict.rationale: Runtime probes show Reclaim's first-party MCP endpoint uses an MCP OAuth flow. It publishes RFC 9728 resource metadata with distinct read, write and mcp scopes, so an agent can be granted a token with limited scope (e.g. read-only). However, no vendor docs describe this, and there is no evidence of user-facing controls for issuing, scoping or revoking agent credentials. missing for 10: vendor documentation of the OAuth/scope model, user-facing scope selection when issuing agent credentials, finer-grained least-privilege scopes beyond read/write, credential revocation/management, independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: a live, auth-gated MCP endpoint on the vendor's own domain speaking the per-spec MCP OAuth flow
